subject: Bridging residency & handback playbook — bespoke retention windows
messages:
From: Cora Patel <cora@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@clearwellhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data handback / retention bridge while we migrate to Redwood Private

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate moving sensitive patient inference workloads to Redwood Private, legal asked me to start the conversation about how retention and final deletion would work during the migration window. We have two immediate asks: one, a short-term "bridging" SLA/order-form we can sign now to cover the 3–6 month migration period while we onboard into our VPC; two, clear deletion certification and timelines once we terminate service.

Key points legal wants to see in writing:
- Hot residency: we need a 90-day hot-access window for active tokens/requests during the migration.
- Cold residency/archive: ability to retain artifacts for up to 3 years for clinical audit reasons, but we want control over how and where that data is stored.
- Deletion timeline: must include a forensic-grade deletion certificate and audit trail within a stated maximum window post-termination.
- Forensic/hold: ability to request an emergency hold for specific datasets for up to 30 days while a regulatory review completes.
- Proof of deletion: evidence (hashes/manifest + timestamped certificate) and optional third-party attestation if required by our compliance team.

Can Redwood provide order-form language that covers these bespoke windows (short-term bridge + longer archival hold), and confirm what you’ll offer for deletion verification and forensic hold process? Also let us know what attachments/artefacts you typically provide (playbooks, safelist, manifest format).

Thanks,
Cora
Cora Patel
Head of Cloud Compliance
ClearWell Health

--

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data handback / retention bridge while we migrate to Redwood Private

Hi Cora — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (Legal/Contracts lead) and Diego (Private deployments engineering) to confirm what we can commit to in an order form vs. what lives in the operational playbook.

High-level response now: yes — we can do a short-term bridging order form that specifies bespoke hot/cold windows during the migration and a set of deletion/attestation deliverables post-termination. I'd like to propose a starting draft for the order form that includes:
- Bridging windows: 90 days hot by default, configurable to 60–120 days via order form.
- Cold/archive retention: up to 36 months with configurable storage class and region locks.
- Deletion commitments: initiation within X business days of termination + full purge of accessible and persistent copies within 90/180/365 days depending on slice (hot/cold/backups) — Vanessa, diego: can you confirm realistic maximums?
- Forensic hold: emergency hold API/contract clause to pause automated deletion for specific dataset identifiers for up to 30 days, extendable by mutual agreement.
- Proof of deletion: timestamped manifest + signed certificate; optional third-party attestation as an add-on.

I'm attaching an initial draft of the retention term language so legal can review. If you can flag the elements that need tighter wording (e.g., exact "initiation" definition or the scope of backups), we'll iterate quickly and share an order-form-ready version.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Partner Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data handback / retention bridge while we migrate to Redwood Private

Thanks Logan + Cora — quick internal notes and a few proposed order-formable commitments below. Diego and I validated the operational implications.

Proposed, order-form language (suggestion):
- "Bridging Hot Window": Redwood will maintain customer live inference residency ('hot') for a contractual bridging term of 90 days following the effective date of the Bridging Order Form. The Customer may elect a bridging hot window between 60 and 120 days at contract signature.
- "Cold Storage Retention": Redwood will retain specified artifacts in cold storage for up to 36 months from creation date. Customer may select storage class (encrypted-at-rest region-locked, or geo-fenced archive) via the Order Form.
- "Deletion Lifecycle and Timelines":
  • Upon termination or expiry of service, Redwood will initiate deletion workflows within 5 business days of written termination notice.
  • Deletion of 'hot' data (active instance/state) will be completed within 30 calendar days of initiation.
  • Deletion of 'cold' archive slices will be completed within 180 calendar days of initiation.
  • Deletion of backups/snapshots will be expunged within 365 calendar days of initiation, subject to snapshot immutability windows noted in the Order Form.
- "Forensic Holds": Customer can issue targeted hold requests (identified by dataset IDs), which pause deletion pipelines for up to 30 calendar days. Extension requests require mutual written agreement; Redwood will provide an audit log of hold actions.
- "Proof of Deletion": Upon completion of purge workflows Redwood will produce a Deletion Manifest containing identifiers, deletion timestamps, and SHA-256 manifests for extracted artifacts, along with a signed Deletion Certificate. Third-party attestation is available as a billable add-on.

Operational notes: Diego — we'll need to tie the deletion initiation to a single canonical signal (signed termination notice + order-form ID) to avoid ambiguity. For the archive deletion cadence, we also need to document retention cutoff vs creation timestamp clearly in the playbook.

I'll attach the safeguard matrix that maps retention slices to storage classes and KMS options.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference

Hi Cora — thank you. Based on Vanessa's suggested language, we've prepared a formal Bridging Order Form and an operational playbook excerpt that maps the timelines above to our deletion pipelines. Highlights:
- Bridging Hot Window: default 90 days (60–120 configurable).
- Initiate deletion within 5 business days of termination notice; hot/cold/backups purges completed within 30/180/365 calendar days respectively.
- Forensic hold: 30-day targeted hold with logged actions and extension by written agreement.
- Proof of deletion: Deletion Manifest + signed Deletion Certificate. Third-party attestation is offered as an add-on.
